Rationale: Downregulating homoserine dehydrogenase reduces drain of aspartate semialdehyde toward threonine/methionine, and lowers intracellular threonine pools, which synergistically weakens feedback inhibition on aspartate kinase.
Partial attenuation of thrB prevents threonine over-accumulation and avoids back-conversion/repressive effects on the aspartate kinase reaction, improving net lysine flux.

Reducing PEP carboxykinase activity prevents decarboxylation of oxaloacetate back to PEP during gluconeogenesis, conserving carbon and energy (ATP) and increasing oxaloacetate availability for the aspartate/lysine pathway.
